# S2. Epidemic phase

We classified each forecast into an epidemic phase based on the change in the final evaluation data over the 28-day forecast period.

For hospital admissions, we compared the 7-day rolling sum of hospital admissions on the forecast date with the 7-day rolling sum 28 days later, for each location and forecast date. A forecast was classified as increasing if admissions increased by more than 15% and by more than 5 admissions, as decreasing if admissions decreased by more than 15% and by more than 5 admissions, and as stable otherwise. The absolute threshold prevents small fluctuations at low counts from being classified as increasing or decreasing. When there were 0 admissions on the forecast date, the percent change is undefined and the phase was based on the absolute change alone.

For wastewater, we classified the phase separately for each wastewater treatment plant and lab. We compared the mean log concentration in the 7 days up to the forecast date with the mean log concentration in the 7 days up to 28 days later, and classified the change as increasing (more than 15%), decreasing (less than -15%) or stable. Sites with no observations in either 7-day window were not classified.

Figure S3. Epidemic phase by forecast date for each location. Top panel: hospital admissions (7-day rolling sum) from the final evaluation dataset, with each forecast date to 7 days later shaded by the hospital admissions phase over the following 28 days. Bottom panels: log wastewater concentrations at each site, shaded by that site's phase.
